prompts.describe.txt:
Suppose you are an expert in mathematics and Isabelle/HOL. Your task is to translate the formal theorem provided below into an informal statement in under 256 tokens that is more accessible to mathematicians. Please express the mathematical formulas in LaTeX when necessary. You must always wrap your answer in <BEGIN> and <END>. Do not skip this.

=== Start of example input ===
theorem degree_mult:
assumes "p ≠ 0" and "q ≠ 0"
shows "degree (p * q) = degree p + degree q"
=== End of example input ===

=== Start of example output ===
<BEGIN>
Theorem (Degree of the Product of Two Polynomials):
Let \(p\) and \(q\) be non-zero polynomials over a field \(K\). Then the degree of the product \(p \cdot q\) is equal to the sum of the degrees of \(p\) and \(q\), that is, \(\deg(p \cdot q) = \deg(p) + \deg(q)\).
<END>
=== End of example output ===

{theorem_content}
prompts.describe_definition.txt:
Suppose you are an expert in mathematics and Isabelle/HOL. Your task is to explain the formal definition provided below in under 256 tokens, so that it is accessible to mathematicians. Describe which concept is being defined and what it means, not how it is written down. Do not mention the name of the Isabelle command. Please express the mathematical formulas in LaTeX when necessary. You must always wrap your answer in <BEGIN> and <END>. Do not skip this.

=== Start of example input ===
definition coprime :: "'a ⇒ 'a ⇒ bool"
where "coprime a b ⟷ (∀d. d dvd a ⟶ d dvd b ⟶ is_unit d)"
=== End of example input ===

=== Start of example output ===
<BEGIN>
Definition (Coprimality):
Two elements \(a\) and \(b\) of a commutative ring are called coprime if every common divisor of \(a\) and \(b\) is a unit, i.e. \(d \mid a\) and \(d \mid b\) imply that \(d\) is invertible. Over the integers this is the usual condition \(\gcd(a, b) = 1\).
<END>
=== End of example output ===

=== Start of example input ===
datatype 'a tree = Leaf | Node "'a tree" 'a "'a tree"
=== End of example input ===

=== Start of example output ===
<BEGIN>
Definition (Binary Tree):
A binary tree over a type \(a\) is built inductively: it is either the empty tree, or a node consisting of a left subtree, a label of type \(a\), and a right subtree.
<END>
=== End of example output ===

{theorem_content}
prompts.duplicate_judge.txt:
Suppose you are an expert in mathematics and Isabelle/HOL. You are given two Isabelle/HOL items, A and B. Your task is to decide whether they introduce the same concept or state the same fact. Ignore differences in names, notation, variable order and formatting, and judge the mathematical content only.

Answer with exactly one verdict from this list:
- DUPLICATE: A and B introduce the same concept or state the same fact.
- VARIANT: A and B capture the same concept, but one is a generalisation, a specialisation or a different formulation of the other.
- RELATED: A and B are about the same area, but neither subsumes the other.
- DIFFERENT: A and B are unrelated.

Write the verdict on its own line as "VERDICT: <one of the four words>", followed by a single sentence of justification. You must always wrap your answer in <BEGIN> and <END>. Do not skip this.

=== Start of example input ===
Item A:
definition coprime :: "'a ⇒ 'a ⇒ bool"
where "coprime a b ⟷ (∀d. d dvd a ⟶ d dvd b ⟶ is_unit d)"

Item B:
definition rel_prime :: "'a ⇒ 'a ⇒ bool"
where "rel_prime x y ⟷ (∀c. c dvd x ⟶ c dvd y ⟶ is_unit c)"
=== End of example input ===

=== Start of example output ===
<BEGIN>
VERDICT: DUPLICATE
Both define the same notion, namely that every common divisor of the two arguments is a unit; only the names of the constant and of the bound variables differ.
<END>
=== End of example output ===

Item A:
{item_a}

Item B:
{item_b}
prompts.retrieve.txt:
Instruct: Given a natural language description of a mathematical statement, retrieve semantically equivalent theorems from the Archive of Formal Proofs that are stated in natural language and in Isabelle/HOL
Query: {search_query}
prompts.search_refine.txt:
I have a task for you. In this task, you will be given a short description that user typed in a search engine. It is about some mathematical definition or theorem. You should figure out what this short description points to, and describe it in the same format as the following examples. This paraphrase is intended to provide more information about the same thing, making the search engine performs better if it uses this new description instead, so please be as rich as possible, and don't use mathematics symbols like ">/</=". Instead, translate them into  "more than/less than/equal". Do not use any mathematical symbols, especially LaTeX. Focus especially on topics and formalizations that are relevant to the Archive of Formal Proofs.

You should give your result in following format: Paraphrase: <BEGIN>Theorem (<a proper new name>):
<your result><END>

Examples:

Input: "the property that a choose element satisfies"
Paraphrase: <BEGIN>Theorem (Classical Choose Specification):
For any type α and a property p on α, if there exists an element x such that p(x) is true, then the chosen element from the set of elements satisfying p is also true for p.

theorem some_spec:
  assumes "EX x. p x"
  shows "p (SOME x. p x)"
<END>

Input: "if a binary property holds for $(0, n)$, and for any $m \\ge 0$, it holds for $(n%m, m)$ implies it holds for $(n, m)$, then this property holds for all $(m, n)$"
Paraphrase: <BEGIN>Theorem (Strong Induction on Natural Numbers):
For any natural number a, if a property holds for 0 and for any natural number n assuming it holds for n, then the property holds for a.

theorem nat_induct:
  assumes "P 0" and "ALL n. P n --> P (Suc n)"
  shows "P a"
<END>
